THIS MFA HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 31.01.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
 JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is posted for admission with the consent of parties the same is taken up for final disposal.
2. This appeal is by the Insurance company challenging the impugned judgment and award dated 15.06.2018 in MVC.No.524/2015 on the file of III Addl.

Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kalaburagi,
whereby the Tribunal partly allowed the claim petition filed by petitioner/claimant, claiming to be the wife of deceased Shivasharanappa Kumbar in a motor vehicle accident dated 30.03.2015 granting compensation in a sum of Rs.7,84,900/- in favour of claimant and respondent No.3 (mother of deceased) in the ratio of 40:60%.
3. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. Petitioner filed the claim petition contending that she is the wife and respondent No.3 is the mother of deceased Shivasharanappa Kumbar.
On 30.03.2015, at about 6.00 p.m, deceased Shivasharanappa Kumbar was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-32/E-8465 ('motor cycle' for short) from Sedam to Peth Sirur village.

While in front of Water Servicing Centre,
near Danibai Layout, Sedam, a lorry bearing registration No.AP-04/TW-1079 ('offending vehicle' for short), came from Kalaburagi side in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
As a result of the accident, deceased sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
As the wife and mother, petitioner and respondent No.3 are entitled for compensation.
As the owner and insurer, respondent Nos.1 and 2 are liable to pay the compensation.

5. Petitioner has pleaded that since respondent No.3 did not join the petitioner in filing the petition,
she is arraigned as respondent No.3.
6. Despite due service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 3 have remained absent and as such placed ex-parte before the Tribunal.

7. Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement disputing the age, occupation and income of the deceased and that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Since the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving license, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
8. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issued.

9. During the enquiry, petitioner examined herself as PW-1 and got Ex.P1 to 6.
10.
Respondent No.2 did not lead any evidence.
11. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.7,84,900/- with interest at 6% p.a.
Further it apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 60-40% between petitioner and respondent No.3.

The details of the compensation granted by the Tribunal is as under:
 Heads Amount  In Rs.
 Towards loss of dependency 6,79,932  Towards Funeral & Transportation 15,000  charges  Towards consortium 40,000  Towards Love and affection 40,000  Towards loss of estate 10,000  TOTAL 7,84,932  Rounded of to 7,84,900  12.
Petitioner has not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
13. However, respondent No.2 has come up with this appeal contending that the judgment and award of the Tribunal is oppose to evidence and material on record and as such not sustainable.
This petition was filed by Neelamma claiming to be the wife of deceased Shivasharanappa Kumbar.
However, respondent No.3, the mother of deceased and her husband filed MVC.No.848/2015 on 12.06.2015, before MACT, Chittapura.
It was partly allowed on 26.11.2016, granting compensation in a sum of Rs.6,52,000/- with interest at 6% p.a.
In the said petition, the petitioners therein claimed that deceased was a bachelor, consequently the present petitioner was not a party to it.

In The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Neelamma W/O Late Shivsharanappa ... on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111025147/
3 fact, petitioners therein filed MFA.No.200957/2017 before this Court seeking enhancement of the compensation.

sentences.text: However, it was withdrawn on 07.11.2017.
Thus, in respect of the accident, two petitions were filed.
MVC.No.848/2016 filed by the parents of the deceased
was disposed of earlier to the present petition.
Consequently, the petition in MVC.524/2015 is liable to be dismissed.

If at all petitioner/claimant is having any claim over the compensation granted in respect of death of Shivasharanappa Kumbar, she is at liberty to claim the same from petitioners in MVC.No.848/2015 and prays to allow the appeal and dismiss MVC.No.524/2015.
14.

Along with the appeal memo, appellant has filed I.A.No.1/2022 to permit the respondent No.2/appellant to produce the following documents:
(1) Copy of payment voucher in MVC.No.848/2015 (2) Exhibits in MVC.No.848/2015 and deposition.
(3) Certified copy of order in MFA.No.200957/2017 (4) Judgment and award in MVC.848/2015 15.
Petitioner/claimant has not filed any objections to this application.

16. Heard arguments of both sides and perused the record.
17.

Thus, respondent No.2/Insurance company has challenged the impugned judgment and award mainly on the ground that in respect of the same accident, compensation was sought by the parents of the deceased in MVC.No.848/2015 and it came to be allowed on 26.11.2016.

In the said petition,
petitioners who are parents of the deceased claimed that the deceased was a bachelor.

However in the present petition, which is filed by one Neelamma claiming that she is the wife of the deceased Shivasharannapa Kumbar, she arraigned the mother of deceased namely, Lalita as respondent No.3 contending that since she failed to join her in filing the petition, she is arraigned as respondent No.3.
However, respondent No.3 remained ex- parte.
Thereby the Tribunal was not in a position to know that in respect of the same accident and death of Shivasharanappa Kumbar, already a petition was filed and compensation has been granted.
It appears respondent No.2/Insurance company was not aware of the fact that already claim petition is filed in respect of the same accident in MVC.No.848/2015.

Only after the award is passed in the present petition i.e., MVC.524/2015, on realizing that there is going to be a double payment in respect of the same accident, they have come up with the present petition.
It appears there is conflict of interest between the present petitioner and the parents of deceased Shivasharanappa Kumbar.
It appears though petitioner was aware of the earlier petition, she did not choose to disclose the said fact.
Anyhow the fact remains that in respect of the same accident, two petitions came to be filed.

Though MVC.No.848/2015 is a subsequent petition, in the circumstances it is inevitable to allow I.A.No.1/2022 and allow the documents pertaining to MVC.No.848/2015 to be placed on record to enable respondent No.2/appellant herein to demonstrate that already claim in respect of death of Shivasharanappa Kumbar is satisfied at the instance of his parents.

The documents produced along with I.A.No.1/2022 prove that already the claim in respect of death of Shivasharanappa Kumbar is satisfied by respondent No.2 and as such it cannot be once again directed to satisfy the claim of the petitioner.

If at all petitioner is the legally wedded wife of deceased Shivasharanappa Kumbar, she is at liberty to claim her share of compensation from the parents of the deceased Shivasharanappa The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Neelamma W/O Late Shivsharanappa ...

In the result the appeal filed by respondent No.2 deserves to be allowed and consequently MVC.No.524/2015 is liable to be dismissed and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal filed by respondent No.2/Insurance Company is allowed.
(ii) Consequently MVC.No.524/2015 is dismissed.

(iii) However, petitioner is at liberty to claim her share of compensation, if any from the parents of deceased Shivasharanappa Kumbar, who are petitioners in MVC.No.848/2015 on the file of III Addl.Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Chittapur, in accordance with law.
